name: warp-text

frames.best_why: The lens is strongest here, bending the middle letters with visible blue and orange fringes.

tagline: Big white headline bends and splits into colour under the cursor.
summary: A heavy single-line headline rendered as a WebGL texture. A lens follows the pointer, bending letters and separating their edges into faint blue and orange fringes; clicks send ripples through the text.
appearance: One wide line of very bold white text on near black, tightly kerned and centred vertically. Near the pointer the strokes lean, stretch and pick up a thin rainbow edge.
behaviour: The lens drifts slowly on its own and snaps toward the pointer when it enters, warping the letters closest to it. Each click pushes an expanding ripple ring through the text.
demo_content: The words "Bend the moment" in a heavy sans font.
use_when: A short, large hero headline should react to the pointer with a physical lens rather than a hover colour.
avoid_when: It needs WebGL and a sized box, works best on one short line, and the effect disappears on touch.
customise: Text, colour, font, weight, size, warp strength and scale, speed, pointer influence, refraction, chromatic split, ripple, lens mode and intro are props.
weight_why: One textured quad in a constant WebGL loop plus a one-off canvas text raster.

a11y.note: The headline is exposed as a labelled image; there is nothing to operate and motion is reduced when requested.

polish_why: Crisp type and a convincing lens; the coloured fringe is faint enough to look like a glitch.
title: Warp Text
